posts.name: Bowie
posts.cooked:
Mocking chiding of Ronway aside, I actually don't mind advice. Especially when everyone acts so fast you're trying not to slow down the roll, you don't notice some cards going down - and you might end up ruining things if not sharp. So having someone pop in with a "You should've pitched this" is more an invite for "Sorry, anyone mind if I play that instead?" and a do-over. It's fine, as far as I think, so long as the delivery of such isn't "WHAT AN IDIOT" and more "This was a better call, and here's why-- ah well!".

There's fine lines, but I love having people's input. I have started hesitating before my play if I have even a moment of doubt, to either ask in chat, or wait for a few votes to show some opinion.

Usually I'm confident; but for global-effects (damage ignores, who should get an SS Tachyon deck-hunt, et cetera) I like a little interaction to make sure I'm not ruining any plans!
